steps.title: Sort cells into lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Sort single cells and multiplets (identified by FSC‑W and FSC‑H gating) directly into 2 µL lysis‑buffer mix per well; immediately seal with seals approved for –80 °C to >100 °C, centrifuge at 2000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, snap‑freeze on dry ice and store at –80 °C until use.

substeps.instruction: Gate singlets vs. multiplets using FSC‑W and FSC‑H (see Figure 1).
Deposit sorted cells into 2 µL lysis buffer per well.
Seal plate with appropriate seals (‑80 °C to >100 °C).

steps.title: Prepare RT master mix
steps.instruction: Make a fresh reverse‑transcription master mix (total 3 µL per well) containing SmartScribe 0.475 µL, RNase Inhibitor 0.125 µL, 5× First‑Strand buffer 1 µL, DTT (100 mM) 0.25 µL, Betaine (5 M, fridge) 1 µL, MgCl₂ (1 M, bench) 0.03 µL, TSO (100 µM) 0.05 µL and H₂O 0.07 µL; dispense 3 µL into each well, cover with fresh film and spin down.

steps.title: Reverse transcription incubation
steps.instruction: Place the RT plate in a thermocycler and run 42 °C for 1 h 30 min, then 70 °C for 5 min, then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare cDNA preamplification mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh cDNA pre‑amplification master mix (total 7.5 µL per well) consisting of 1 µL RT reaction, 5 µL H₂O, 1.0688 µL Kapa HiFi HotStart ReadyMix (2×), 0.125 µL IS‑PCR primer (10 µM), 0.05625 µL Lambda Exonuclease (total 7.5 µL); dispense 7.5 µL into each well (final reaction volume 12.5 µL), spin down and cover with a new lid.

steps.title: cDNA preamplification PCR
steps.instruction: Run the following thermocycler program: 37 °C 30 min (Lambda exonuclease, 1 ×), 95 °C 3 min (initial denaturation, 1 ×), 98 °C 20 sec, then 18–24 cycles of 67 °C 15 sec (annealing) followed by 72 °C 4 min (elongation), finish with 72 °C 5 min (final elongation) and hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: SPRI bead cleanup of cDNA
steps.instruction: Using a 20 % PEG‑8000 SPRI‑bead solution, add 0.7 × the reaction volume (e.g., 8.75 µL for a 12.5 µL reaction) to each well, mix by pipetting, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on a magnetic stand for 3 min, remove supernatant, add 40 µL 80 % EtOH, incubate 30 sec, remove EtOH, repeat EtOH wash, air‑dry beads 10–15 min, remove plate from magnet, elute in 15 µL EB or TE buffer, mix, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on magnetic plate 3 min, and optionally transfer the supernatant to a clean elution plate.

steps.title: Quantify cDNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: In a flat‑bottom black 96‑well plate add 97 µL 1× Qubit HS dsDNA solution, then 3 µL cDNA sample, add standards (8‑step ladder 0–10 ng/µL in TE), read on a plate reader (485 nm excitation, 528 nm emission) and calculate cDNA concentration.

steps.title: Optional cDNA quality control
steps.instruction: Assess cDNA fragment size distribution using an Agilent High‑Sensitivity 5000 DNA chip (or equivalent) on a Tapestation.

steps.title: Dilute cDNA to target concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute each cDNA sample in water to achieve a final concentration of 150 pg/µL in a total volume of 15 µL, based on the average Qubit measurement.

steps.title: Prepare Tn5 tagmentation master mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh Tn5 master mix (total 1.8 µL per reaction) containing Nuclease‑free H₂O 1.05 µL, TAPS‑PEG buffer (50 mM TAPS, 25 mM MgCl₂, 40 % PEG‑8000) 0.5 µL, and psfTn5 (Addgene #79107) loaded with 50 µM MEDS‑A/B adapters 0.25 µL; note that the TAPS‑PEG buffer is viscous and should equilibrate to room temperature before use. Dispense 1.8 µL into each well of a new tagmentation plate.

steps.title: Add normalized cDNA to tagmentation
steps.instruction: Add 0.7 µL of cDNA (normalized to 150 pg/µL) to each well containing the Tn5 master mix, vortex to mix, cover with a new lid and spin down.

steps.title: Tn5 tagmentation and stop
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 55 °C for 10 min, then immediately stop the reaction by adding 1 µL per well of 0.1 % SDS, vortex, spin down and incubate 7 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Make a fresh PCR master mix (total 19.5 µL per well) containing H₂O 1 µL, 2.5× buffer 13.25 µL, dNTPs 5 µL, KAPA 0.75 µL, and KAPA 0.5 µL (exact composition as listed); dispense 19.5 µL into each well of the tagmentation plate (which already contains 3.5 µL sample).

steps.title: Add primers and set up PCR
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL of indexed primers (from 384‑well index plates, 3.75 µM each forward and reverse) to each well (final volume 25 µL = 3.5 µL sample + 19.5 µL PCR mix + 2 µL primers), vortex, spin down and cover.

steps.title: PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Run the following thermocycler program: 72 °C 3 min (gap fill, 1 ×), 95 °C 30 sec (first denature, 1 ×), 95 °C 15 sec (denature, 12 ×), 67 °C 30 sec (annealing, 12 ×), 72 °C 45 sec (extension, 12 ×), final extension 72 °C 4 min, hold at 4–10 °C.

steps.title: Pool amplified libraries
steps.instruction: Transfer 2.5 µL from each well into a single 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: SPRI bead cleanup of pooled library
steps.instruction: Add 0.9 × the pooled library volume of SPRI‑bead solution, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on magnetic rack 3 min, remove supernatant, wash twice with ≥1 mL 80 % EtOH (30 sec each), air‑dry beads 10–15 min, resuspend in 100 µL EB or TE, place on magnetic rack 3 min, transfer supernatant to a new tube, repeat the entire cleanup (steps 1‑7) and elute in 30 µL EB or TE; optionally place on magnetic rack 3 min and transfer the final eluate to a new tube.

steps.title: Optional library QC
steps.instruction: Assess the final library on an Agilent High‑Sensitivity D5000 TapeStation (or equivalent) to verify fragment size distribution.

steps.title: Bioinformatic preprocessing
steps.instruction: Trim adapters and low‑quality bases from raw reads, align RNA‑seq reads to the reference genome with STAR, remove duplicate reads with Picard, and generate a transcript‑level counts file using HTSeq.

steps.title: Run CIM‑seq analysis
steps.instruction: Provide CIM‑seq with four inputs: (1) raw gene‑count matrix (genes as rows, samples as columns), (2) ERCC spike‑in count matrix, (3) a dimensionality‑reduced representation of the data, and (4) a class label for each singlet; generate the reduced representation and class labels using Seurat (see SatijaLab tutorials).

steps.title: Install CIM‑seq software
steps.instruction: Download CIM‑seq from https://github.com/EngeLab/CIMseq or install directly in R with devtools::install_github("EngeLab/CIMseq"); the vignette is located at https://github.com/EngeLab/CIMseq/tree/master/vignettes.
